classification.difficultyReason: Combine exact intercept calculations with labelled sketches of upward- and downward-opening parabolas.

content.prompt: Sketch the parabolas. In each case, determine the $x$- and $y$-intercepts and the vertex of the parabola.

answer.worked:
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(0)^2+1\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept and vertex are $(0,1)$; the axis of symmetry is $x=0$. Since $2x^2+1\geq1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. The parabola opens upwards and passes through $(1,3)$ and $(-1,3)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with its vertex above the x-axis and an additional labelled point.
spec.mathematics: y=2x^2+1; vertex and y-intercept (0,1); point (1,3); no real x-intercepts.

answer.worked:
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=4(0)^2-1\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(0,-1)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$. For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}4x^2-1&=0\\4x^2&=1\\x^2&=\frac14\\x&=\pm\frac12\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards through $(-\frac12,0)$, $(0,-1)$ and $(\frac12,0)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with exact root labels and labelled vertex.

answer.worked:
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=6(0)^2-1\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(0,-1)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$. Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}6x^2-1&=0\\6x^2&=1\\x^2&=\frac16\\x&=\pm\frac1{\sqrt6}\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens upwards through $(-\frac1{\sqrt6},0)$, $(0,-1)$ and $(\frac1{\sqrt6},0)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with exact surd root labels and labelled vertex.

answer.worked:
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-2(0)^2+8\\y&=8\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(0,8)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$. Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-2x^2+8&=0\\2x^2&=8\\x^2&=4\\x&=\pm2\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens downwards through $(-2,0)$, $(0,8)$ and $(2,0)$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with both roots and its maximum labelled.

answer.worked:
When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-2(0)^2+9\\y&=9\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(0,9)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$. Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-2x^2+9&=0\\2x^2&=9\\x^2&=\frac92\\x&=\pm\frac3{\sqrt2}\\x&=\pm\frac{3\sqrt2}{2}\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens downwards through $(-\frac{3\sqrt2}{2},0)$, $(0,9)$ and $(\frac{3\sqrt2}{2},0)$.
